items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: I've talked to Mark Hazel about it

ctx.x: Maybe so. Yes. That's what holds the price down, the reissue boys.

Oh, yes. But, of course, some of them have never been found. There are some cylinders, like of a legendary figure, Buddy Bolden. We know about him from the people who played with him, the people who heard him, but no one's ever found this cylinder. Emmett Hardy, too, from New Orleans. Buddy Bolden was from New Orleans, too. Yes. Emmett Hardy was one of the people that they named as a possible influence on Big Spiderbeck, who Johnny mentioned before. I believe there must be something to that, because I've talked…
It's supposed to be a cylinder, you know, just like a Buddy Bolden.

items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: Diaz, who played a beautiful jazz piano, and Monk Hazel was on drums.

ctx.x: You can tell us a little bit about that.

He was a piano player, a very good piano player, by the name of Diaz, who afterwards went to New York and played commercial music, and I guess he made a lot of money, and I don't blame him for playing commercial music. Hooray for him. He wasn't going to get stuck with this damn fool jazz business, you know, give your soul away and get nothing back. The hell with that. Diaz, who played a beautiful jazz piano, and Monk Hazel was on drums. Elry Mazin on clarinet, much to his disgust, since he was a saxophone player,…
